record.original_question: Show that the absolute complexity C(gamma(t)) of any L2 geodesic gamma(t) in D_mu^s(M) is bounded above by an exponential function of time and initial H^s speed.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $M$ be a smooth, closed, oriented Riemannian manifold of dimension $n$, and let $\mu$ be its Riemannian volume form. For a Sobolev exponent $s > n/2 + 1$, denote by $\mathcal{D}^s_\mu(M)$ the group of volume-preserving diffeomorphisms of $M$ of Sobolev class $H^s$. This group is a smooth infinite-dimensional Hilbert manifold, and it carries the right-invariant $L^2$ (Arnold) metric whose geodesics describe solutions of the incompressible Euler equations on $M$.

For a curve $\gamma:[0,T]\to \mathcal{D}^s_\mu(M)$, define its absolute complexity $C(\gamma(t))$ to be the total spatial complexity accumulated by $\gamma$ up to time $t$ (for instance, measured by the growth of an appropriate geometric quantity such as the length of the image of a generic submanifold, or equivalently a measure of the intricacy of the configuration $\gamma(t)$ relative to the identity).

Prove that there exist constants $a, b > 0$, depending only on $M$ and $s$, such that for every $L^2$-geodesic $\gamma(t)$ in $\mathcal{D}^s_\mu(M)$ with initial velocity $\dot\gamma(0)\in T_{\mathrm{id}}\mathcal{D}^s_\mu(M)$,
$$ C(\gamma(t)) \;\le\; a\, \exp\!\bigl(b\, t\, \|\dot\gamma(0)\|_{H^s}\bigr) $$
for all $t$ in the interval of existence of $\gamma$.
